say: The tickets sold out within an hour of going on sale.
stem: Which sentence means the same as what you heard?
choices: Demand for the tickets was very high.
The tickets were cheaper than expected.
The sale started an hour late.
Only a few tickets were available online.
explanation: Selling out within an hour means demand was very high.

say: I'd rather not take the early train, if that's all right.
choices: The speaker prefers a later train.
The speaker missed the early train.
The speaker has no preference.
The early train has been cancelled.
explanation: "I'd rather not" shows a preference against the early train.

say: The results were far from what we had predicted.
choices: The results were very different from the prediction.
The results were close to the prediction.
The prediction was made far away.
The results took a long time to arrive.
explanation: "Far from what we had predicted" means very different.

say: Hardly anyone turned up to the first meeting.
choices: Very few people came to the first meeting.
Most people arrived late.
The first meeting was cancelled.
Nobody was invited to the meeting.
explanation: "Hardly anyone" means very few people.

say: The course isn't cheap, but it's worth every penny.
choices: The course is expensive but good value.
The course is cheap and good.
The course costs a penny a day.
The course is not worth the cost.
explanation: "Worth every penny" means good value despite the price.

say: We'll have to postpone the trip until the weather improves.
choices: The trip will be delayed.
The trip is cancelled for good.
The trip will go ahead in bad weather.
The trip will be shorter.
explanation: To postpone is to delay to a later time.

say: Not many people realise how much water is used to make a pair of jeans.
choices: Most people are unaware of the water used in making jeans.
Jeans need to be washed often.
Many people know how jeans are made.
Jeans are made without water.
explanation: "Not many people realise" means most people are unaware.

say: The figures for last year were roughly the same as the year before.
choices: The figures stayed fairly stable.
The figures rose sharply.
The figures were not recorded.
The figures fell slightly every month.
explanation: "Roughly the same" means stable.

say: It's the first time the event has been held outside the capital.
choices: The event has always been in the capital until now.
The event has never been held before.
The capital will host the event next time.
The event moves to a new city every year.
explanation: First time outside the capital means it was always in the capital before.

say: You can't use the gym unless you've had an induction session.
choices: An induction session is required before using the gym.
The gym is closed during induction sessions.
Induction sessions are optional.
The gym is only for staff.
explanation: "Can't ... unless" sets a requirement.

say: The building is due to be completed by the end of the year.
choices: The building should be finished this year.
The building was finished last year.
The building work has not started.
The building will be demolished.
explanation: "Due to be completed" means it is expected to be finished.

say: Surprisingly, the cheaper model outperformed the expensive one.
choices: The cheaper model worked better.
The expensive model was better.
Both models were equally good.
The cheaper model sold more.
explanation: To outperform is to do better.

say: Few of the original features of the house have survived.
choices: Most of the original features have been lost.
The house has many original features.
The house was rebuilt from nothing.
The original owners survived.
explanation: Few survived means most were lost.

say: The talk was aimed at people with no background in science.
choices: The talk was for non-specialists.
The talk was for scientists.
The talk was about the history of science.
The talk had no clear aim.
explanation: No background in science means non-specialists.

say: Attendance has doubled since we moved the class to the evening.
choices: Twice as many people come now.
Half as many people come now.
The class is now twice as long.
The class moved twice.
explanation: Doubled means twice as many.

say: I couldn't have finished the project without my supervisor's help.
choices: The supervisor's help was essential.
The supervisor did not help at all.
The project is not finished.
The speaker helped the supervisor.
explanation: "Couldn't have ... without" means the help was essential.

say: The number of visitors fell for the third year running.
choices: Visitor numbers have dropped three years in a row.
Visitor numbers fell by three.
Visitors stayed for three years.
Visitor numbers rose after three years.
explanation: "For the third year running" means three years in a row.

say: The council is considering a ban on cars in the old town.
choices: A car ban has been proposed but not decided.
Cars are already banned in the old town.
The council has rejected a car ban.
Cars must park in the old town.
explanation: "Considering" means not yet decided.

say: Applicants should have at least two years' experience in a similar role.
choices: Two or more years of relevant experience is required.
Exactly two years of experience is required.
No experience is needed.
Applicants will train for two years.
explanation: "At least two years" means two or more.

say: The noise from the building site made it almost impossible to concentrate.
choices: It was very hard to focus because of the noise.
The building site was quiet.
The speaker works on a building site.
The noise helped the speaker relax.
explanation: Almost impossible to concentrate means very hard to focus.

say: We underestimated how long the survey would take.
choices: The survey took longer than expected.
The survey was quicker than expected.
The survey was not finished.
The survey was too long for participants.
explanation: Underestimating the time means it took longer than expected.

say: The scheme was so successful that it has been extended to other cities.
choices: The scheme now runs in more places.
The scheme has ended.
The scheme was tested in other cities first.
Other cities refused the scheme.
explanation: Extended to other cities means it runs in more places.

say: Unlike most of her colleagues, she prefers to work from home.
choices: Most of her colleagues prefer working at the office.
All her colleagues work from home.
She dislikes working from home.
Her colleagues often visit her home.
explanation: "Unlike most of her colleagues" means they prefer the opposite.

say: The guide book is out of date, so don't rely on the opening times it gives.
choices: The opening times in the book may be wrong.
The book has no opening times.
The attractions are all closed.
The book was written recently.
explanation: Out of date means the information may be wrong.
